name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_SEQUENCING_MCQ_Q01 - Sequential steps in test tube baby program

questiontext.text:
In an in vitro fertilisation and embryo transfer (IVF-ET) procedure under the 'Test Tube Baby' programme, arrange the following operational steps in the correct chronological sequence:

A. Induction of zygote formation by fusing gametes under simulated laboratory conditions
B. Cleavage division of the zygote to form an early embryo containing up to 8 blastomeres
C. Collection of mature ova from the wife/donor and motile sperms from the husband/donor
D. Transfer of the early embryo into the fallopian tube (ZIFT) for subsequent development

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The 'Test Tube Baby' programme relies on in vitro fertilisation (IVF) followed by embryo transfer (ET), which proceeds through sequential laboratory and clinical phases: gamete harvesting, in vitro fertilization, cleavage development, and anatomical transfer.

Step 2: Analysis of Sequential Events
• First, viable gametes must be procured: mature ova are retrieved from the female partner or donor, and semen containing motile spermatozoa is collected from the male partner or donor.
• Second, the collected gametes are brought together in a controlled culture medium under simulated physiological conditions in the laboratory to induce fertilization and form a diploid zygote.
• Third, the fertilized zygote is cultured in vitro to undergo initial mitotic cleavage divisions until it forms an early embryo possessing up to 8 blastomeres.
• Fourth, this early embryo (containing up to 8 blastomeres) is clinically introduced into the fallopian tube of the female via zygote intra fallopian transfer (ZIFT) to complete gestation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct chronological sequence begins with the collection of mature ova and motile sperms, followed by the induction of zygote formation under simulated conditions, then the cleavage division of the zygote to form an early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres, and concludes with the transfer of the early embryo into the fallopian tube.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_SEQUENCING_MCQ_Q02 - Chronological sequence of reproductive health milestones

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following historical milestones and demographic events in reproductive health and population dynamics in the correct chronological order (from earliest to latest):

A. Enactment of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act by the Government of India
B. National initiation of comprehensive 'family planning' action programmes in India
C. Statutory legalisation of Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) with strict conditions in India
D. The population of India crossing 1.2 billion with an annual population growth rate under 2 per cent
E. Global population reaching 6 billion while the population of India reached close to the 1 billion mark

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
National reproductive healthcare policies, statutory abortion frameworks, and census demographic transitions in India have unfolded along a distinct historical timeline over the post-independence era.

Step 2: Chronological Verification of Events
• National family planning programmes were initiated in India in 1951, making India one of the earliest countries to adopt reproductive health as a national social goal.
• The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act was passed and legalized by the Government of India in 1971 to reduce illegal abortions and curb maternal mortality.
• By the year 2000, explosive demographic growth caused the global population to reach 6 billion (up from 2 billion in 1900), while India's population escalated close to 1 billion.
• According to the May 2011 Indian Census, India's population crossed 1.2 billion (while global population reached 7.2 billion), registering a growth rate of less than 2 per cent (20/1000/year).
• The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act was enacted in 2017 to amend gestation limits and specify medical practitioner opinion requirements.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct chronological sequence proceeds from the launch of national family planning programmes (1951), followed by the legalisation of MTP (1971), then the world population reaching 6 billion with India near 1 billion (2000), then India crossing 1.2 billion in the census (2011), and finally the enactment of the MTP Amendment Act (2017).
